articles.title: $80 million rich 6-foot-10 new Kings star could earn $3.5 million in his big NBA return after a one-year hiatus
articles.summary: NBA News: Ben Simmons hasn't played an NBA game in over a year, and Sacramento just bet $3.5 million that the time off actually worked. The Kings signed the thr.
articles.body: Ben Simmons hasn't played an NBA game in over a year, and Sacramento just bet $3.5 million that the time off actually worked. The Kings signed the three-time All-Star to a one-year, non-guaranteed deal, with real money riding on whether he's still good enough to stick.The number that's getting astonishing hype is $1 million. That's what Simmons pockets simply for making the Kings' roster when they open the season against the Clippers on October 21. Everything else in this contract is built around him earning a spot, not keeping one.How much money will Ben Simmons make in his new Kings tenure?According to NBA reporter Michael Scotto, Simmons' deal tops out at $3.5 million, but it's non-guaranteed, which means Sacramento can move on without much cost if the comeback stalls. Scotto reported Simmons "will earn $1 million" once he survives cuts and reaches opening night.That's the first checkpoint. Everything past it depends on whether a 30-year-old who has battled back and leg problems for years can hold up over an 82-game season. Simmons has a staggering net worth of $80 million, as per Celebrity Net Worth.What role is Sacramento actually giving him?Simmons is set to back up rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr, the Kings' No. 7 pick, though ESPN and Andscape's Marc J. Spears reported he could end up guarding all five positions depending on matchups. Spears also relayed that people close to Simmons see him as someone who could stay in Sacramento past this season if things click, since he's "a pretty loyal guy" by nature.Simmons spent his year away working on his back and leg injuries and even bought a 50 percent stake in a South Florida fishing club. He told Men's Health he needed distance from the game, saying, "I needed to get away, and have some space, and just find myself again."Does Simmons still have anything left in the tank?Former NBA champion Richard Jefferson isn't ready to write him off. Speaking to ESPN Australia, Jefferson argued "Ben has the talent to be an All-Star this year" if his body cooperates. That's a big if. Simmons hasn't looked like an All-Star since 2020-21, when he averaged 14.3 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists a game in Philadelphia.Since then, back surgeries and nerve pain have limited him to just 108 games, and his final stretch with the Nets and Clippers last season produced only 5.0 points and 4.7 rebounds a night. The Kings aren't expecting that version of Simmons back overnight. They're hoping a healthier body and a smaller stage give him room to rebuild.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “I was really stubborn in my earlier..”: How Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry’s motherhood journey became a powerful reminder of just how strong a mother can be
articles.summary: NBA News: Motherhood has given Ayesha Curry some of her happiest moments, but it has also tested her in ways that were difficult to hide. Her third pregnancy in.
articles.body: Motherhood has given Ayesha Curry some of her happiest moments, but it has also tested her in ways that were difficult to hide. Her third pregnancy in 2018 brought repeated hospital stays, severe sickness and exhaustion while she was preparing to welcome another child with Stephen Curry. Years later, those experiences helped her understand motherhood differently.By 2024, Ayesha was expecting her fourth child and looking back at those earlier pregnancies with a different perspective. She had learned that being a strong mother was not about doing everything herself. Sometimes, it meant knowing when to slow down, accept help and give herself some grace. Ayesha Curry pushed through five hospital stays, severe sickness and a difficult road to motherhoodAyesha’s third pregnancy became difficult almost from the start. In February 2018, she explained that she was dealing with hyperemesis gravidarum, a severe pregnancy condition that can cause prolonged nausea, vomiting and exhaustion.The symptoms also took away something that meant a lot to her. Ayesha had built a career around food, yet she could barely eat or cook. In a Feb. 2018 blog post, she wrote, “For the past 4 months, I've barely been able to eat let alone cook. The mere smell of food averts me.” She admitted that the situation had put her “in a funk” and added, “I am truly very, very sad.”The struggle did not disappear quickly. On April 6, 2018, Ayesha revealed that she had already spent five hospital stays since the beginning of the year. Giving an update on Instagram, she wrote, “I've had 5 hospital stays since the New Year and have pretty much been sucking at life.” She then added that she felt she was finally starting “to turn a corner.”That was a brutally honest look at what she was going through. Yet Ayesha kept moving forward and eventually welcomed her son Canon on July 2, 2018. The baby arrived earlier than she and Stephen expected, turning a painful pregnancy chapter into one of the family's biggest moments.But another health challenge followed. On October 5, 2018, Ayesha underwent surgery to remove her thyroid and a cyst. From her hospital bed, she shared an update that simply read, “All went well. God is good. Thank you for your prayers.”Two days later, Stephen Curry also reassured reporters. After the Warriors' open practice at Oracle Arena on October 7, he was asked about Ayesha and said, “We’re good,” before adding, “Thanks for asking.” Ayesha Curry eventually learned that asking for help could make motherhood easierThose experiences clearly stayed with Ayesha. When she became pregnant with her fourth child in 2024, she approached motherhood with a much different mindset.In an interview published on March 1, 2024, Ayesha admitted, “I was really stubborn in my earlier pregnancies. And that hurt me in the end. It made things really hard on me.” She then explained the lesson those experiences had taught her: “I had to learn to put my pride aside and realize it was okay to take help, to have people around me help and to not shy away from it.”That was not just about pregnancy. Ayesha had started thinking differently about motherhood as a whole. She explained that she could not do everything alone and said, “I know I can’t do this alone, it truly takes a village.”She also spoke about how that village keeps changing. “There’s always people coming in, people leaving, and people here forever. And that’s okay,” Ayesha said in 2024.That is where her story becomes more than a celebrity pregnancy story. Ayesha went through severe sickness, five hospital stays, childbirth and surgery, but she did not come away believing that strength meant carrying every burden herself.Instead, she learned to accept support.As for Ayesha, that may have been the biggest lesson of all. A mother can be strong while admitting she needs help. In fact, sometimes that honesty is exactly where her strength begins.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown’s Nigeria boxing appearance creates 76ers contract concerns after unexpected “I did 0 prep” admission
articles.summary: NBA News: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown has drawn attention after a video showed him boxing in Nigeria during the offseason. Combat sports account Happy .
articles.body: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown has drawn attention after a video showed him boxing in Nigeria during the offseason. Combat sports account Happy Punch shared the footage on September 10, showing Brown wearing gloves and headgear in a ring, along with clips of his training and basketball career. The post also included Brown’s comment: “I did 0 prep for this.” Brown was traded from the Boston Celtics to the 76ers in July.Jaylen Brown’s Nigeria boxing video and 7uice Foundation tripThe footage shows Brown inside a ring in Lagos in front of a crowd. He is seen wearing boxing gloves and headgear while facing an opponent, although details about the other person, the format of the event and whether it was a formal exhibition have not been reported.The video was shared by Happy Punch, which described the appearance as Brown’s boxing debut. However, Yardbarker noted that Brown had already taken part in a friendly boxing session in Morocco earlier this summer, so calling the Nigeria appearance his first time boxing would not give the full picture.Brown was in Nigeria as part of work connected to his 7uice Foundation. His foundation has focused on youth, education and community opportunities, and Brown has continued that work while preparing for his first season in Philadelphia. The Nigeria trip included meetings and community activities before the boxing footage surfaced.What caught many fans’ attention was Brown’s own comment about the lack of preparation. “I did 0 prep for this,” he wrote alongside the video. That line became a major part of the reaction because Brown is not only a professional basketball player but also one of the NBA’s highest-paid stars.Brown’s move to Philadelphia was one of the biggest NBA trades of the summer. The 76ers acquired him from Boston in exchange for Paul George and draft picks. NBA.com confirmed the trade on July 6. Brown had spent his entire first 10 NBA seasons with the Celtics, winning the 2024 NBA championship and Finals MVP award during that run.Jaylen Brown’s boxing family and 76ers contract concernsBoxing is familiar territory in Brown’s family. His father, Quenton Marselles Brown, known as Marselles Brown, was a professional heavyweight boxer who finished his career with a 33-18-1 record and won the World Boxing Union heavyweight title in 2016. Brown’s grandfather, Willie Brown, also had a professional boxing background.Jaylen Brown has also been open about his own interest in combat sports. He trains in Muay Thai and has spoken about possibly trying boxing or UFC after his basketball career. In February, he said he had discussed the idea with UFC CEO Dana White and would like to explore combat sports at some point.For now, though, Brown remains focused on basketball. That is why the Nigeria footage has raised questions about the risks of boxing while he is under contract with Philadelphia.Yardbarker reported that the standard NBA player contract includes a clause covering activities that carry a serious risk of injury, with boxing specifically listed among the activities that can require team permission. Neither Brown nor the 76ers had publicly commented on the Nigeria video when the report was published.The timing also matters. Brown is entering his first season with Philadelphia, and the 76ers will expect him to be ready for the new campaign. The Nigeria video does not show an injury, but it has still given fans another reason to question how much risk Brown should take during an important offseason.For now, the clearest facts are simple: Brown boxed in Nigeria, he said he had done no preparation for it, and the exact details of the event have not been made public.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Team USA coach Kara Lawson speaks out on prognosticators after dominant FIBA World Cup win over Hungary
articles.summary: Kara Lawson dismissed FIBA's power rankings after Team USA women's basketball demolished Hungary 108-56 in the World Cup quarterfinal match.
articles.body: Team USA women’s basketball coach Kara Lawson dismissed outside opinions after the Americans routed Hungary 108-56 in the FIBA Women’s World Cup quarterfinal Thursday. During the postgame press conference, Lawson was asked if a recent power ranking provided her team with any added motivation entering the final stage of the tournament. Lawson admitted she did not know about the ranking, but addressed those who may have more confidence in France, which appeared to be the more dominant team during group play. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "This is a big tournament, this is the World Cup, and it’s okay for people to have opinions on who they think is going to win and who they think is going to lose and who they’re cheering for and who they’re going to boo. That’s a competition, I think that’s why we love sport, it’s why it’s so exciting," Lawson said. "And now in this moment in women’s basketball you have more people than ever before that are giving their opinions and they’re making rankings and they’re doing that. That’s all great, we clearly don’t talk about any of that inside our bubble, and we really just focus on what we need to do. ITALY WOMEN'S BASKETBALL STAR TEARS INTO REF AFTER MISSING GAME-TYING SHOT VS US IN WOMEN'S WORLD CUP "Worrying about someone else’s opinion doesn’t serve you, because it doesn’t change whether you can do it or not. It’s just someone’s opinion." FIBA moved France ahead of the United States in its final "Smart Power Rankings" following the group stage. The Americans fell to second after narrowly escaping Italy with a 55-52 victory, their lowest-scoring World Cup performance since the introduction of the 3-point line in 1984. CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK The ranking also described the Americans’ on-court connections as a "work in progress." However, FIBA included a disclaimer stating that its rankings were "entirely subjective" and did not constitute an accurate ranking system. "As far as France, what a wonderful team, and they’ve had an outstanding World Cup so far, so they should have a lot of people thinking they can do well," Lawson said. France strengthened its case Thursday with a 90-61 quarterfinal victory over China. The French remain on the opposite side of the bracket, meaning they could only face the United States in the championship game. One of the biggest factors affecting the outlook for Lawson’s team entering the knockout stage was concern over the starting lineup. Lawson did not directly address that debate following Thursday’s victory. WNBA LEGEND BREANNA STEWART OPENS UP ON REPRESENTING AMERICA AT FIBA WOMEN'S WORLD CUP Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese once again came off the bench against Hungary. Lawson instead started Chelsea Gray, Jackie Young, Kahleah Copper, Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart. Lawson's commitment to keeping her veteran starting lineup has drawn frustration from fans, especially on Wednesday after Lawson suggested to OutKick that she will be keeping the veteran lineup going into the final stage. Still, the lineup worked against Hungary with obvious results. The U.S. scored 36 points in the opening quarter and carried a 59-30 advantage into halftime. The Americans shot 59% from the field, made 12 of their 23 3-point attempts and recorded 31 assists on 40 baskets. Their 108 points were the most ever scored in a Women’s World Cup quarterfinal, while they became the first team to record at least 30 assists at that stage of the tournament, according to FIBA. Collier led the Americans with 19 points and six rebounds. Every player on the U.S. roster scored, and five finished in double figures. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Clark narrowly missed her second double-double of the tournament, recording 10 points and a game-high nine assists in 20 minutes. Reese contributed nine points, six rebounds and three assists, while Bueckers added seven points and three assists. The victory also extended the Americans’ World Cup winning streak to 34 games. The program has not lost in the tournament since falling to Russia in the 2006 semifinals. The U.S. will face the winner of Thursday’s quarterfinal between Australia and Spain in Saturday’s semifinal. Lawson’s team is now two victories away from securing a fifth consecutive World Cup championship.

articles.title: Project B league signs more WNBA players, surpassing 20-name milestone
articles.summary: More WNBA players have signed to Project B as the basketball league grows. Here's who's on board.
articles.body:
Project B is slowly unveiling more WNBA names for the league's inaugural season, which starts in January 2027.

On Thursday, the global basketball organization announced six more athletes who plan to play. The latest wave includes 2024 WNBA champion Betnijah Laney-Hamilton and the No. 9 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft Angela Dugalić ( Washington Mystics ), four-time all-star Brionna Jones ( Atlanta Dream ) and former Florida State standout Makayla Timpson ( Indiana Fever ). The list also includes two-time FIBA Women's EuroBasket champion Antonia Delaere ( Minnesota Lynx) and two-time Olympic medalist Valériane Ayayi ( Phoenix Mercury ).

"I've always believed in competing with purpose and being part of something bigger than yourself," Laney-Hamilton said in a release. "What excites me about Project B is the chance to compete with some of the best players from around the world while also having a real voice in what we're building. It's an opportunity to help shape something new for the game, and I'm excited to be part of it from the beginning."

2026 WNBA season is underway. See photos from the league's 30th year

The six bring Project B's list of WNBA players to 22 as the league approaches training camp in Seoul, Korea, from Jan. 6-12, 2027.

Other WNBA players who have signed with Project B include Azzi Fudd and Alanna Smith of the Dallas Wings , Alyssa Thomas of the Mercury, Awa Fam of the Seattle Storm , Jewell Loyd of the Las Vegas Aces , Jonquel Jones of the New York Liberty , Kamilla Cardoso of the Chicago Sky , Nneka Ogwumike of the Los Angeles Sparks and Kelsey Mitchell and Sophie Cunningham of the Fever.

"Project B is bringing together incredible players from around the world and creating something that gives us a real opportunity to help shape what comes next," Jones said. "I'm excited by the level of competition, but also by the chance for players to have a meaningful voice and stake in what we're building. I'm looking forward to being part of it from the beginning."

The concept for Project B is to have two separate leagues ― men and women ― with six teams, each with 11 players. Those teams will compete in a global circuit slated to kick off in Jan. 2027 and run through April 2027. Each city will host a 10-day event, crowning a city champion, and those victories will count towards a season-long championship. To date, Project B has revealed it will play in Tokyo, Japan and Valencia, Spain.

Every athlete who plays in Project B is expected to have equity in the league. Project B hasn't disclosed any salaries yet, but a league spokesperson previously told USA TODAY Sports they are "higher than anything you've ever seen in women's sports."

Project B has a host of investors in the league, including women's basketball legends Cheryl Miller, Candace Parker and Lauren Jackson and NFL Hall of Fame quarterback Steve Young. Additionally, the league has secured Host Broadcast Services (HBS) to be the official broadcaster for the league's inaugural circuit . HBS has broadcast the FIFA World Cup since 2002. The games will stream live on YouTube.

articles.title: USA and France ease into women's Basketball World Cup semis
articles.summary: The United States breezed into the semi-finals of the Women's Basketball World Cup with a commanding 108-56 win against Hungary on Thursday.The Americans and...
articles.body:
The United States breezed into the semi-finals of the Women's Basketball World Cup with a commanding 108-56 win against Hungary on Thursday.

Napheesa Collier topscored with 19 points while Caitlin Clark delivered nine assists and added 10 points in a dominant quarter-final performance in Berlin from the nation seeking a fifth consecutive title.

The Americans and their roster packed with WNBA stars will face either Spain or Australia in the semi-finals on Saturday and they remain on course to play the team they beat in the 2024 Olympic final, France, in the gold medal game.

Having survived a scare from Italy, who pushed them all the way in their second pool game before the Americans won 55-52, the USA have gone from strength to strength in the tournament in Germany.

On Thursday they raced into a 36-12 lead in the first quarter, effectively ending the game as a contest.

France comfortably beat China 90-61 in the day's second quarter-final to move into the last four.

WNBA star Xu Han led all scorers with 21 points, but her contribution was not enough for the Chinese to contend with a superior French team.

Zhang Ziyu, China's towering 2.23 metre (7ft 4in) teenage centre, played 18 minutes and scored seven points, but at 19 she has shown in this tournament that she has a bright future.

Janelle Salaun and Marine Johannes both scored 15 points for France and US-born Gabby Williams added 14 points.

The French will meet Germany in the semi-finals after the host nation defeated Belgium 93-74, despite a 29-point performance from Belgian power forward Emma Meesseman.
